works.title: Tokopedia's Product Launching Platform
works.description: Built a cross-platform design system used across Shopee, Garena, and SeaMoney.

columns.html: Overview
A Project to create a self-serve product launching platform that helps sellers/brand to create their own campaign on their shop.
Objective
The main objective is how to create a seamless platform that sellers can use to make their process of product launching campaign simpler and easier.
🎉 Outcome
An end to end self serve product launching platform is now available to the selected seller in Tokopedia
Bring x times (confidential) higher traffic to brands & Tokopedia as a platform compared to the usual Flash Sale campaign
Total of thousands of products sold out in an (x mins - confidential) in a single campaign
👩‍💻 My Role
Main User Experience Designer for this project
Co-assist a co-design session which involved ~20 people from different function (Business, Product, Engineer, Data Analyst) to help align our vision for the product.
Collaborate and worked together with PMs, Engineer, UI Designer to help bring the design to life
Designed the end to end journey and user flow on the seller's end
Conducted user testing & user in-depth interview on end to end journey.
⚡️ Behind The Product
Project Background
In the first quarter of 2020, Tokopedia has been given the opportunity to work together with some of the most highly requested official brands.

The collaboration was formed to provide these brands with a reliable online platform to launch their products. Considering that the products that they launch have always been a huge hit among collectors and fans of the brand & public, where they usually only lasted 10 - 30 mins before all the products sold out. This collaboration has successfully increased traffic and conversion for both parties.
After the big success of launching and partnering with these brands, we receive a surge in interest from other brands to also have a product launch on our platform.
Key Problem
The sudden surge of interest from brands also comes with some challenges that we need to solve. Since the first iteration of Tokopedia's product launching has to be done manually:

Long time to process and a campaign request from brands A brand needs to wait for several days to launch their product due to manual operational effort. This makes the platform isn't scalable for future business opportunities with brands.
Can’t run multiple launching brands at the same time Since it was done manually, the process will take up too many people & effort to run.

There's a special request from brands to have specific terms and condition An example of this use case is many brands needed to limit/give exclusivity for some of their campaigns. With this request, there's an additional couple of hours for the operational team to validate this rule.

There's no specific entry point where sellers can request to create their product launching campaign Currently, sellers would have to manually reach out to our internal team to request this type of campaign.

works.title: The Village I Didn't Know I'd Left Behind
works.description: They say it takes a village to raise a child. Nobody warns you how quiet it gets when you've moved away from yours.

blocks.html: They say it takes a village to raise a child. Nobody warns you how quiet it gets when you've moved away from yours.

When I became a mom abroad, I imagined the usual picture: grandparents dropping by, an aunt offering to hold the baby while I showered, a friend sitting across from me with a cup of tea saying, "Yes, it's hard. You're doing fine." Instead, it was me, my husband, and a very small human who needed us every minute of every day.
The Loneliness Nobody Talks About

Being a mom far from home is a particular kind of lonely. It isn't that you're never around people. You're surrounded by a baby's needs all day long. But there's no one who knows you, who remembers you from before, who can look at your face and tell you haven't slept.
The hardest moments aren't dramatic. They're small and repetitive:
Standing in the kitchen at 3 p.m. with a toddler on your hip, wishing someone would just walk in and take over for ten minutes.
Scrolling through family group chats and seeing everyone gathered for a celebration you're missing.
Feeling guilty that your child is growing up without cousins and grandparents in the room.
Realizing you haven't had a full conversation with another adult in days.

There's also a quiet grief in it. You miss your mom. You miss being mothered yourself. You miss the version of parenting where someone else knows the answers, or at least reassures you that you're allowed not to.
There Is No Sick Leave in Motherhood
Nothing shows how alone you are like getting sick.
When you have a village, being unwell means someone shows up. Your mom takes the baby for the afternoon, or a sister brings soup and stays for a few hours. You get to lie down and just be sick.

When you don't, you're running a fever while warming a bottle. You're nauseous and still chasing a toddler who has no idea you feel awful. Your body wants to stop, but there's no one to hand the baby to, so you keep going. Your child still needs breakfast, a diaper change, a nap routine, and bedtime stories, whether you slept or not.

Even when your husband takes over after work, the daytime hours are still yours. No email to your manager and no "I'm out today" message can make your job pause, because this job never clocks out. You just get through it, and often you get through it alone.
The Guilt Makes It Heavier

Then comes the second layer: guilt. You chose this move, this adventure, this life abroad. So who are you to complain? Many of us swallow the exhaustion because it feels ungrateful to say it out loud.

But two things can be true at once. You can love your life abroad and find motherhood without a village really, really hard. Missing your people doesn't mean you made the wrong choice. It means you're human.
What Has Helped Me (and Might Help You)
I can't build a village overnight, and neither can you. But I've learned that small, deliberate choices can make the days lighter. Here are the three that matter most to me.
🙋‍♀️ Ask your partner to cover a few times a day

This isn't about splitting chores or getting the laundry done. It's about giving you time that belongs only to you. Ask your husband or partner to take over for a short stretch, even 20 to 30 minutes, a few times a day. Use it to sit in silence, drink a hot coffee, shower without rushing, or stare out of a window.

The rule is that this time isn't for the house. It's not for errands, dishes, or meal prep. It's for you. And on the days you're sick, this is your version of sick leave: ask for the cover, and take it without guilt.
Say it out loud, because partners can't read your mind. "I need a break, can you take over for a bit?" is a complete and reasonable sentence.
🏋️‍♀️ Move your body: workout, good mood

I used to think exercise was a luxury I'd get back to "when things settle down." Then I realized it's one of the fastest ways to shift my mood on a hard day. It doesn't have to be a big production. A short home workout, a run, or a walk with the stroller can clear your head and give you a little bit of yourself back.
Some days it feels like the last thing you have energy for. Those are usually the days it helps the most. Workout, good mood. It's simple, and it works.
📱 Video call your people, and do it often

Distance is real, but so is technology. Schedule regular video calls with your mom, your sister, your best friend, anyone who makes you feel like you. Let them see your messy hair and your toddler's chaos. Let them make funny faces at your child.
It won't replace a hug, but it does remind you that you're not as alone as it feels. And it lets your child build a relationship with faraway family, even if it's through a screen.
You're Doing Better Than You Think

If you're a mom living abroad reading this in the middle of a long, lonely day, I hope you know that you're not failing. You are doing an enormous job with fewer hands than most people get. That's not a small thing.

Be gentle with yourself. Ask for the break. Move your body. Call the people who love you. And if you can, find one or two other moms nearby who are in the same boat. Sometimes a village starts with just one friend.
You may not have the village you grew up in, but you can build a smaller one, one call, one break, and one honest conversation at a time. 💛

intro: I'm Nadya Arizka a product designer based in Singapore with 9 years of experience in product design.

I have developed a passion for user interface and user experience design. I've always enjoyed engaging with people and discovering the secrets to people's relationships with technology which attracted me to learn more about user experience and fell in love with it more each day.
I received a Bachelor's degree in Information Technology. As an IT graduate, knowing basic knowledge about product development has helped me to understand the feasibility of products that I design.
